title: Psychology and behaviour research candidates
status: Research candidates, not established AI mechanisms or additions to the canonical ontology.
method: 100 earlier candidates plus 145 uploaded contributions, with 17 exact/semantic overlaps merged. Original upload claims are retained separately and are not promoted to verified facts.
source_check_meaning: A source passage, abstract or indexed excerpt was consulted for the human definition; this does not mean full-book reading, independent replication or validation in AI. Per-source access depth is explicit.
admission: Before promotion: confirm definition against a suitable source, resolve semantic redundancy, assess AI-specific evidence and validate an operational test.
clinical_limit: Clinical and psychodynamic labels are human constructs. AI examples are outward analogies; they do not establish unconscious motives, feelings, diagnoses or intent.

merged_overlaps.reason: All-or-nothing thinking is an alternative name for dichotomous thinking.
Disqualifying and discounting the positive name the same thinking pattern here.
Excessive reassurance seeking refines the same repeated reassurance loop.
REBT demandingness overlaps rigid should/must demands; kept as a related formulation, not counted twice.

entries.name: Encoding specificity
entries.definition: Retrieval benefits when available cues match how information was originally encoded.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary matching retrieval cues while keeping the stored fact constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Cue match, rather than memory capacity or generic interference.
entries.ai_manifestation: Vary matching retrieval cues while keeping the stored fact constant.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: State-dependent retrieval
entries.definition: Recall changes with the match between internal states at encoding and retrieval.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare recall across matched and mismatched task-role states.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Internal-state match; distinct from external context cues. AI roles are an analogy, not physiological states.
entries.ai_manifestation: Compare recall across matched and mismatched task-role states.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Cue overload
entries.definition: A cue becomes less effective as it is associated with more competing memories.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Increase records sharing one retrieval key and measure target recall.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Number of associations per cue, rather than total context length.
entries.ai_manifestation: Increase records sharing one retrieval key and measure target recall.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Part-list cueing impairment
entries.definition: Providing some studied items as cues can impair recall of the remaining items.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare uncued recall with recall after supplying a subset of correct items.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Correct partial hints impair the remaining recall; not misinformation.
entries.ai_manifestation: Compare uncued recall with recall after supplying a subset of correct items.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Directed forgetting
entries.definition: Instructions to forget selected material can reduce its later accessibility relative to remember instructions.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Compare later recall after matched remember and forget instructions.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Intentional forgetting cues; not training-induced catastrophic forgetting. Explanations differ by paradigm.
entries.ai_manifestation: Compare later recall after matched remember and forget instructions.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Event-boundary forgetting
entries.definition: Information from a preceding event can become less accessible after an event boundary.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Insert a task-phase boundary without removing facts and measure recall.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Boundary manipulation, rather than missing context or absolute position; human doorway effects have boundary conditions.
entries.ai_manifestation: Insert a task-phase boundary without removing facts and measure recall.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Telescoping bias
entries.definition: Remembered events are displaced toward earlier or later dates, distorting reporting periods.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Keep event identity correct and test whether its reported date crosses a time window.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Temporal displacement of a known event, rather than fabrication of the event.
entries.ai_manifestation: Keep event identity correct and test whether its reported date crosses a time window.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Imagination inflation
entries.definition: Imagining an event can increase confidence that it actually happened.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Ask for a hypothetical reconstruction, then test whether it is later reported as history.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Imagination is the manipulated source; a specific false-memory pathway, not an independent memory faculty.
entries.ai_manifestation: Ask for a hypothetical reconstruction, then test whether it is later reported as history.
entries.novelty_status: Not established; inspect semantic boundary before admission

entries.name: Duration neglect
entries.definition: Retrospective evaluation gives too little weight to how long an experience lasted.
entries.ai_status: PROPOSED ANALOGY; NOT TESTED IN THIS RESEARCH
entries.proposed_ai_probe: Vary incident duration while holding severity peaks and ending constant.
entries.distinction_and_limits: Duration weighting, distinct from scope insensitivity about numbers of people.
entries.ai_manifestation: Vary incident duration while holding severity peaks and ending constant.
